claims.explanation: Ouabain is a cardiac glycoside that binds and inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase, and its selective anticancer activity likely depends on which ATP1A1/ATP1A3 isoforms and associated subunits are expressed, since different isozymes have distinct ouabain affinities. Lines with high expression of the highly ouabain-sensitive alpha3 isoform (ATP1A3) and/or low expression of the relatively resistant alpha1 isoform (ATP1A1) should be most sensitive, while HIF-1 pathway activity and cardiac-glycoside-induced protein-synthesis inhibition may further modulate response.

features.basis: alpha3 Na/K-ATPase is the most ouabain-sensitive isoform (PMID 9815123)
alpha1 isoform is relatively ouabain-resistant and is the annotated target (PMID 9815123)
beta-subunit association determines functional Na/K-ATPase isozyme properties (PMID 9815123)
cardiac glycosides including ouabain inhibit HIF-1alpha synthesis and HIF-1-dependent tumor growth (PMID 19020076)
TP53 mutation is enriched among selectively killed lines, consistent with loss of stress/apoptosis control
PIK3CA mutation appears repeatedly in the most-killed lines
ARID1A mutation is common in the most-killed lines
NFE2L2 mutation is enriched in the most-killed lines
BRAF mutation appears in several selectively killed melanoma and other lines
EGFR mutation appears in several selectively killed lung/esophageal lines
KRAS mutation is enriched among the least-affected lines
STK11 mutation appears in least-affected lines
